# Avatar

A letter avatar showing the first character of a name. The name picks one of five tones (blue, green, orange,
purple, cyan) in a stable way (light background with dark text, dark background with light text in dark mode),
without a border; with an icon instead of text, the background is a neutral fill. It can have an accent ring
and a status badge at the bottom right. The avatar itself is hidden from screen readers (the name is usually
shown next to it); only the status badge is announced.

**Category**: Basic · **Common uses**: Avatars of conversations, teams and projects; `leading` of list items; account menus; online status

## Import

```ts
import { Avatar } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Shows the first character of the name and picks one of five tones from the name, so the same name has the same
color everywhere. Common sizes are 20, 28 and 32.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Inline } from 'vellum-ui'

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <Inline gap={3}>
      <Avatar name="Design" size={20} />
      <Avatar name="Alex Morgan" size={28} />
      <Avatar name="Sam Lee" />
      <Avatar name="Jordan Kim" />
      <Avatar name="Taylor Reed" />
      <Avatar name="Riley Chen" />
    </Inline>
  )
}
```

## Variants

### Ring and icon

`ring` adds an accent ring for avatars that should stand out, such as teams or the current user; `icon` shows an
icon instead of text (for example, system notifications) on a neutral fill.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Inline } from 'vellum-ui'

export function RingAndIcon() {
  return (
    <Inline gap={3}>
      <Avatar name="All members" ring />
      <Avatar name="System notifications" icon="bell" />
      <Avatar name="System notifications" icon="bell" ring />
    </Inline>
  )
}
```

### Status badge

`status` takes a tone of StatusDot and appears at the bottom right; `statusLabel` is its accessible name.

```tsx
import { Avatar, Inline } from 'vellum-ui'

export function WithStatus() {
  return (
    <Inline gap={3}>
      <Avatar name="Alex Morgan" size={32} status="success" statusLabel="Online" />
      <Avatar name="Sam Lee" size={32} status="warning" statusLabel="Away" />
      <Avatar name="Casey Brooks" size={20} status="neutral" statusLabel="Offline" />
    </Inline>
  )
}
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Person's or item's name: the first character is shown, and the whole name determines the tone in a stable way (the same name has the same color everywhere). | — | Yes |
| `size` | `number` | Size in pixels: commonly 20 (tables, tags), 28 (sidebars) or 32 (lists). | `32` | No |
| `ring` | `boolean` | Accent ring, for avatars that need to stand out, such as teams or the current user. | — | No |
| `icon` | `IconName` | Shows an icon instead of text (such as system notifications), on a neutral fill without a tone. | — | No |
| `status` | `StatusDotProps['tone']` | Status badge at the bottom right (a StatusDot tone), such as online status; not shown when omitted. | — | No |
| `statusLabel` | `string` | Accessible name of the status badge, such as "Online"; the default name of the tone is used when omitted. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.

## Types

Types of this library used above. Import them with `import type { … } from 'vellum-ui'`.

### IconName

Name of a registered icon. Only the icons listed here can be used; they are Lucide icons under shorter names
(`trash` is Lucide's `Trash2`, `more` is `Ellipsis`). All names at runtime: `iconNames`.

118 values, listed on the [Icon](Icon.md#types) page.

### StatusDotProps

Props of StatusDot.

| Field | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `'success' \| 'warning' \| 'danger' \| 'neutral' \| 'accent'` | Tone: `success` for normal, `warning` for attention, `danger` for errors, `neutral` for inactive, `accent` for reminders. The caller maps business meanings (online, running, disabled, and so on) to tones and describes them with `aria-label`. | — | Yes |

### BaseProps

Accessibility and test props shared by all layout primitives (and, partly, by other components): `testId`,
`aria-label`, `role` and `id`, rendered on the root element.
